chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Preferring the Casa Manana to the Palladium
summary: He liked the Casa Manana best and lists other Los Angeles ballrooms such as Casino Gardens, the Aragon and Trianon.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, I lost the Palladium, but I don't consider it a loss, because at that time there were so many other ballrooms in California that actually paid just as good or better money. I used to like the Casa Manana better
than anyplace to play in. It was such a warm room and good feeling bandstand to play on and the crowd was great.
And there was no problem, they didn't object to mixed personnel?

Oh, no. They had a bunch of swinging dancers there. I mean that's what they wanted to do. You know, it was great for a jazz band to play at. Whereas the Palladium, you had to play everything, you know. The Casa Manana I loved. And then of course Tommy had the Casino Gardens - - Dorsey. We played there. We played the Aragon before Welk ever saw the place. We used to play out at Horace Heidt's Trianon Ballroom, and we played a place downtown, the Avadon, but -- they didn't lose anything, except possibly the -- you know, saying that you were able to play the Palladium, which was kind of famous. But I later played it and without any problems. So I don't figure I lost anything.
